label: GO: rises with unrewarded streak x p(a2), growing late in episode; D2: lower when policy favours a1
terms: (phase == GO) * ((prev_reward == 0) + (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) + (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * (tv("reward", -3) == 0)) * (ep_trial / 100) ** 3 / (1 + np.exp(choice)) ;; (phase == GO) * ((prev_reward == 0) + (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) + (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * (tv("reward", -3) == 0)) / (1 + np.exp(choice)) ;; (phase == D2) * np.maximum(choice, 0) ;; (phase == D2) * np.minimum(choice, 0) ;; (phase == D2) * table(prev_state, {1: 1, 2: -1}) ;; (phase == GO) * table(prev_state, {1: 1, 2: -1}) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D2) * (common == 0) * table(state, {1: 1, 2: -1})
explanation: Raw update gate z of unit 36. Timing dominates (R^2 1.00): near 0 at D1/GO and ~0.82-0.96 at D2, all rising late in the episode. Beyond timing: (1) at GO it spikes (up to ~0.5 vs ~0.08 baseline) when the agent has a run of unrewarded trials (count of consecutive r=0 over the last 1-3 trials) and its policy favours a2 (p(a2)=1/(1+exp(choice))); the effect grows steeply with episode trial (cubic in ep_trial/100), plus a smaller non-time-scaled version and a bump when the unrewarded previous trial reached S1 (e.g. after a2 S1 u). (2) at D2 it is lower when the policy logit favours a1 (strongest slope for choice>0), higher when the previous trial reached S1 than S2, and slightly higher after a rare transition into S1 (a2->S1) than into S2 (a1->S2). D1 residual is negligible. Value and hidden good state add little. Uses only observed inputs plus the model policy (no future variables). Dev R^2 beyond timing 0.60, test 0.58 (all ceiling 0.64, all-observed 0.51).

issues: The 'unrewarded streak (count of consecutive no-reward trials over last 1-3)' claim is a numpy artifact. In the terms, (prev_reward==0) + (A)*(B) + ... is boolean +/* on arrays, which numpy evaluates as logical OR/AND, so the expression reduces to just (prev_reward==0). Evidence: the GO term with the 'streak' scores exactly the same as (phase==GO)*(prev_reward==0)*(ep_trial/100)**3/(1+exp(choice)), test 0.14834 in both cases. A real numeric count (1.0*...) does slightly worse: 0.1452 alone and 0.5812 in the full set versus 0.584. Separate streak indicators add only about 0.008 (0.148 -> 0.156). So 'streak' should not be in the label.

The GO spike is systematically under-predicted. In misses, every worst-fit window is a late-episode (t71-t99) GO step after unrewarded a2 trials where actual z is 0.3-0.56 and the prediction is 0.07-0.18 (e.g. t85 0.453 vs 0.112, t86 0.559 vs 0.114). p(a2) = 1/(1+exp(choice)) caps out at 1, so it cannot follow how strongly the logit favours a2. An unbounded shape scores better: (phase==GO)*(ep/100)^3*(prev_reward==0)*max(-choice,0) gets test 0.185 versus 0.148 for p(a2).

The claim about the smaller GO term that does not scale with time is weak. Its weight is 0.009 against 0.094 for the time-scaled term, and on its own it scores 0.098, mostly through overlap with the main term.

The D2 claims hold. D2 choice terms alone give test 0.376; adding the prev_state S1-vs-S2 term gives 0.415. The rare-into-S1 term adds about 0.003 (0.563 -> 0.565), and a full action x state table at D2 does slightly better (0.585).
Reproduced the agent's scores: test 0.584. No future variables are used at GO. At D2, action, state and common are already observed.
